text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Does the pain feel like it is coming from his hip area as well, or is it strictly isolated to the knee? Have you noticed any difficulty with internal rotation of his left hip when he moves?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: It is very common for hip pain to present as knee pain in children due to shared nerve pathways. I would like to examine his hips now; can you ask him to lie flat while I check the range of motion in both legs, specifically looking for limited internal rotation on the left?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: The patient is in the second grade, lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco or known toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text: I will now perform a physical examination of his hips to check for limited internal rotation, which is a key sign of hip pathology. I will also look for any tenderness or swelling in the hip joint itself.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent illness, rash, weight loss, change in appetite or urinary symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The absence of systemic symptoms like fever, weight loss, or recent illness makes infectious or malignant causes less likely, pointing toward a mechanical or inflammatory issue. I will now examine the hips to see if limited internal rotation confirms hip pathology referred to the knee.
